summary: Ep 64 is Toei's Sagittarius-temple trial gauntlet (the crushing roof, the flooded cavern, the cliff Seiya cannot climb — none of it in the manga) wrapped around the CLOSE of ch 38, and that close is the chapter's own title beat. Ch 38 (our 109-chapter space; en-WP's inflated list numbers it 039 '少年たちよ！女神を託す') opens with the Sagittarius Cloth firing its arrow at Seiya — ep 63's final scene, already anchored — and its climax is the arrow striking the wall, the hidden Greek inscription, Aiolos's testament 'To the young men who have come here, I entrust you with Athena's life', and Hyoga rejoining the party. Ep 63 stops at the arrow's flight; ep 65 opens inside the House of Capricorn. So ep 64 is the SOLE adaptation of ch 38's testament pages, and they are the chapter's load-bearing reveal — the sole-adaptation exception is satisfied in both halves, mixed STANDS, and the row carries the anchor (which is the point: filler would falsely mark those pages never-adapted). Ep 64 -> END 38 [START 38] v11, ending mid-chapter, so the continue is IN 38 (C1) — ch 38's back half (the dash through Capricorn, the crack, Shura's appearance) is played next, at ep 65.

annotations.note: weight: significant — because it is a resolution, not a fragment: the Aiolos testament is ch 38's own title beat (ep 64's JP title 少年よ！君たちにアテナを託す is the chapter title 少年たちよ！女神を託す, ja-WP + en-WP chapter list), it closes the Sagittarius house, it restores the four Saints and it reunites Hyoga with the party for the rest of the Twelve Houses. NEW material, not a duplicate: ep 63 ends on the arrow being fired and ep 65 opens inside Capricorn, so these pages are adapted NOWHERE else in the run. SOLE-ADAPTATION EXCEPTION, both halves stated: (1) the pages appear in no other episode — checked against every stored anchor around it (ep 63 -> 38 [37], ep 65 -> 39 [39]); (2) the beat is a major plot point of the source — the reveal of Aiolos's dying message and the arc-node it closes. Mixed therefore stands and the row carries the anchor. Refines the stored partial {38}, whose batch-17 note still reads 'ch 39' in Wikipedia's pre-N22 phantom +1 space.

The whole middle of the episode — the second arrow-hole passage, the crushing roof Shiryu holds back, the flooded cavern Hyoga stops, the cliff-swing Shun gives up to Seiya, the warm Cosmos that restores all four, the teleport back to the temple — is Toei's own; the manga has the arrow strike the wall and expose the testament directly, with Hyoga simply walking in from Scorpio. Anime-original material inserted INSIDE an adapted chapter; it is what makes the row mixed rather than canon, and it moves no position.
